sources.entry: CalDAV and CardDAV protocol servers and web clients/interfaces for Electronic calendar, address book and contact management.

summary.name: CardDAV
summary.one_liner: CardDAV (vCard Extensions to WebDAV) is an IETF address book protocol, published as RFC 6352, for accessing and sharing contact data on a server.
use_cases: sharing an address book with other users
connecting iOS contacts to a server
accessing Gmail contacts from third-party clients
summary.what_it_does: CardDAV is an address book client/server protocol that lets users access and share contact data stored on a server. It is built on WebDAV, which runs over HTTP, and uses vCard as the format for contact data. The protocol was developed by the IETF and published as RFC 6352 in August 2011, with the specification proposed by C. Daboo of Apple Inc. An October 2013 update added support for higher-resolution contact images and lower data consumption. The page lists ports 80 and 443 as the protocol's ports.
notable: Published as IETF RFC 6352 in August 2011
Built on WebDAV and HTTP, uses vCard data
Became a sync protocol in iOS 7 and is supported by Gmail, replacing ActiveSync there
October 2013 update for higher-resolution contact images
caveats: The page does not state licensing terms; pricing is inferred as open source from the IETF standard, so it may be better marked unknown
